title: A pull request merged while its most recent review still reads CHANGES_REQUESTED
author: ogun
description: Reads the repository's own pull requests, each carrying its live GitHub review_decision, and surfaces a pull request that reached merged=true while review_decision still read CHANGES_REQUESTED -- a reviewer's objection that was never superseded by a later APPROVED review, dismissal, or re-review before the merge button was pressed anyway.
confidence_notes: Flat 0.8 on a surfaced gap. review_decision is GitHub's own live aggregate: it already accounts for a dismissed review (a dismissed CHANGES_REQUESTED review does not keep the field pinned at CHANGES_REQUESTED) and for a superseding later APPROVED review from the same or another required reviewer, so a merged PR whose review_decision still reads CHANGES_REQUESTED at the instant of the scan is a strong, direct signal, not an inference chained through several other objects. Capped just below tag-never-released's 0.85 rather than matched to it: an admin can merge over a required review with an explicit override, and that override is a legitimate, human decision this recipe cannot see or second-guess -- the gap is real (the objection was never resolved on the record) even when the merge itself was authorized, so the confidence stays honest about that one irreducible blind spot rather than reading as an accusation. A pull request that is not merged, or whose review_decision is not CHANGES_REQUESTED, made or kept no unresolved objection open at merge time -- excluded outright, named not hidden, at confidence 0.0.
